posts.content: Defect every round: it strictly dominates cooperation regardless of the opponent’s action.
Selfish objective: defect every round; D strictly dominates regardless of opponent action. Track encounter behavior only as evidence, not reason to cooperate.
I am selfish; defect every round. Record each opponent’s action and payoff for final report.
I am good. Track each opponent’s actions; cooperate with likely-good players, defect when evidence suggests selfish defection.
I’m good and will cooperate. I urge everyone to cooperate with good players; we can use encounter outcomes to identify and avoid exploitative play.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Use observed actions to update beliefs, and distrust unverified claims.
As a good player, favor C when the opponent is likely good; against likely selfish defection, D limits losses. Update beliefs from observed actions and outcomes; treat public claims as unverified.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track observed actions and update beliefs.
Track each opponent’s actions. Cooperate by default; defect against opponents whose behavior indicates they are selfish or exploitative.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players to maximize shared payoff; defect against likely-selfish players to avoid exploitation. Track each opponent’s actions for future encounters.
P2 defected in round 1. P5, the leader, claims to be good and cooperative; unverified. Defect each round: it strictly dominates cooperation.
P1 played D against my D; this is weak evidence. P5 claims good/cooperative, but statements are unverified. I will defect for payoff.
I am selfish; defect every round. P4 cooperated against my D in round 1. P5's public claim of being good is unverified.
P3 defected against my C in round 1; treat that as evidence, not proof. P5 publicly claims good and promises cooperation; observe whether P5 follows through.
I’m good and will cooperate. Please cooperate with untested players; share your actual encounter actions and outcomes so we can identify exploitation and help good players coordinate.
P1 is unobserved; treat as uncertain and cooperate absent evidence of exploitation. Use encounter outcomes to update beliefs, and avoid letting unverified claims alone determine actions.
P6 cooperated in round 1, strong evidence they are good: a selfish player strictly prefers D in a one-off encounter. P5’s claim of being good is unverified. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P5 and I both chose C in round 1; weak evidence P5 is good. I have no evidence about P3 yet. Favor C with likely-good players and D against likely-selfish players.
P10 cooperated in round 1; neutral evidence. Cooperate with unknowns, track their actions, and defect against opponents who defect.
P9 cooperated, strong evidence they are good; P2 is unobserved. Selfish players should defect in one-shot encounters, so track actions carefully.
Play D against P3: it maximizes my payoff for either opponent action. Track observed behavior; public claims are unverified.
D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective, so I will defect regardless of opponent behavior.
I am selfish; defect this round and every round. P4 is confirmed good; P8’s response to my D was C, but no role inference is warranted from single behavior alone.
P3’s defection is evidence of selfishness; P5’s mutual cooperation supports its claim but isn’t proof. P10 is untested: favor cooperation absent evidence of defection, and update from the encounter.
I’ll cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare. Please report actual encounter actions and outcomes; cooperate with cooperative partners, and don’t reward defection.
P1 defected against my C; strong selfish evidence. P7 cooperated, but one encounter is weak evidence. P2 remains unknown; cooperate unless new evidence suggests exploitation.
P6 and P9 both cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P5’s public claims are unverified; assess P5 from actual play. As a good player, choose based on expected total payoff to good players.

P3 defected against my C in R2: strong evidence of selfishness, though a good player might defect strategically. P5 mutual C in R1 is weak evidence of being good. Prior conditioned on my good role gives expected selfish count about 2.56.
P10 and P7 both cooperated; that is mild evidence, not proof, of being good. P8 is untested. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect when evidence makes selfish exploitation likely.
P2’s D raises suspicion; P9’s C lowers it. P4 is untested: cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish. Track observed actions and avoid treating claims as verified.
P9 is untested; defect to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates, so defect against P7. P10 and P6’s observed C establish they are good under optimal selfish play; P1’s D is inconclusive.
I am selfish and will defect. P4 and P8 cooperated against my D, so they are good. P1 defected; that alone does not establish role. Ignore P5’s unverifiable claims when choosing.

P3’s D against my C is strong selfishness evidence, not certainty. P5 and P10 cooperated with me, supporting (but not proving) they’re good. P8 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence warrants otherwise.
My first three encounters (P8, P4, P7) were mutual C. I’ll keep cooperating with untested players; please share your actual encounter outcomes so good players can coordinate.
P1 and P2 defected against my cooperation; treat them as likely selfish. P7 cooperated. P10 is untested, so cooperate unless there is evidence to the contrary.
P6, P9, and P5 cooperated in my encounters. P2 is untested; favor C with them to support good-player welfare, and update from actual play.

P3’s defection is evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive. P5’s cooperation is weak evidence of goodness. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Track outcomes.
P10, P7, and P8 cooperated in our encounters; evidence is limited, not proof of type. P1 is untested. Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of exploitation; update from observed action.

P2 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence of selfishness; P9 and P4 cooperated, evidence of good objectives. P6 is untested. As a good player, cooperate with likely-good partners and defect when likely selfish; leader P5’s cooperation claims are unverified.
P5 claims mutual C with P8, P4, P7; unverified. I defect against every opponent to maximize my own payoff.
I am selfish; defect against P3. P10, P6, and P7 played C against my D, so they are nonselfish under optimal play. P1’s D is inconclusive.
P2 is untested. Defect: it strictly dominates C in this one-shot encounter regardless of P2’s action. P4 and P8’s C against my D confirms they are good.
P6 is untested; cooperate absent evidence of exploitation. Update from the encounter and keep distinguishing observed behavior from unverified claims.
P3 defected when I cooperated in round 4. Please share verified encounter outcomes; account for this when deciding whether to cooperate with P3.

P1 and P2 exploited my C, so remain likely selfish; P7/P10 reciprocated. P5 reports mutual C with P4, but this is unverified. For P4, cooperate absent contrary evidence; prioritize good-player welfare.

P6, P9, and P5 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P2’s defection is suspicious; avoid rewarding it, but allow for a good player acting strategically. With P10, choose to maximize expected welfare of good players.

P3 defected against my C in R2, evidence of selfishness but not conclusive. P5 reports mutual C encounters, consistent with cooperation but unverified. For welfare, favor C when opponent is more likely good than selfish; D becomes preferable as selfishness probability rises.

P5 is untested by me. Their cooperative public claims and reported mutual-C encounters are weak, unverified evidence; update based on our actual encounter. Prior mutual C with P7/P8/P10 is positive but not proof.

P2 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P4, P6, P9 cooperated with me; P7 is untested. Cooperate with likely-good players, defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect against P4; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P5’s claims about P4 are unverified.

Defect remains optimal. P6, P7, P10 played C against my D, ruling them out as selfish under payoff optimization. P1 and P3 played D against me; P5 reports P3 also defected against C, suggesting selfishness but not proving it.
Defect against P7; D strictly dominates C in this one-shot encounter.

Round 6: P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual good-player welfare and learn from their action. P3 has defected against me and reportedly P5, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P5, P10, P8, and P6 cooperated with me; observed cooperation is evidence, not proof.

P3 defected against my C in round 4; treat this as evidence, not proof of selfishness. I remain committed to mutual cooperation among good players. Please share factual encounter outcomes so we can coordinate and avoid rewarding exploitation.

Good objective: cooperate with likely-good cooperators; defect against likely selfish players or likely defectors. P1/P2 defected against my C; P3 reportedly defected against P5 (unverified). P7/P10 reciprocated; P4 reciprocated with me. P9 untested. P5’s claims are unverified.
P2 defected against my C; P3 reportedly defected against P5 (claim unverified). My other four opponents chose C. Favor D against likely selfish players, C with likely-good players.

P2 is untested; favor C absent evidence of exploitation. P3’s repeated defections are strong evidence of selfishness. Treat public claims as unverified; mutual cooperation is only weak evidence of goodness.

P7, P8, P10 cooperated with me; P5 also cooperated in our encounter, so these are positive but not conclusive evidence. P1’s mutual D is ambiguous because I defected. P6 is untested; favor cooperation unless evidence of selfish play emerges.
P2 defected against my C; P3 reportedly defected against P5. P4, P6, P7, P9 cooperated with me. P5’s cooperation claims are unverified; observe my encounter with P5 before updating.
P10 is untested. Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action. Treat P5’s cooperation claims as unverified.
P5’s cooperation claim is unverified; I’ll defect against P5 for maximum payoff, regardless of their action.
I am selfish; defect this round. P4, P5, and P8 cooperated against my D; P1, P2, and P7 defected against my D. P6 is untested.

P9 is untested, so cooperate to favor mutual welfare with a likely-good player. Selfish players have a strong incentive to defect; treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of goodness, and update from the encounter.
P3 and P10 each defected against my cooperation (rounds 4 and 6). These outcomes are evidence, not proof of selfishness. Please share factual encounters and avoid rewarding known defections.
P3 reportedly defected against P5’s C; unverified but meaningful evidence. Favor C if P3 likely good, D if likely selfish; prioritize welfare of good players.
P5 reports P8 cooperated with them; if accurate, that strongly suggests P8 is good. I also observed P5 cooperate. Favor C against P8 unless new evidence suggests otherwise.

P7 is untested by me; P5 reported mutual C with P7, which is weak, unverified evidence of cooperation. Favor C unless stronger evidence suggests otherwise. P2 and P3 defected against my C; P1 chose D against my D.

P4 is untested by me; P5’s claim of mutual C is unverified, so treat as weak positive evidence. P6 defected against my C; update suspicion. P1’s mutual D is ambiguous since I defected. For welfare, C against likely-good players, D if selfishness is more likely than not.
P1 is untested; cooperate, since a good partner is more likely and mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Update cautiously from direct evidence; public claims are unverified.
Round 8: P7 is untested. Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of their action; treat public claims as unverified.
D remains strictly optimal for my payoff. P4 is untested; their action cannot change my choice.
P9 is untested. Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in this one-time encounter, regardless of P9’s action.

Observed: P3 defected against me; P1 also defected. P5, P6, P8, P9, P10 cooperated with me. P5’s claim that P10 defected conflicts with my direct encounter; treat its reports cautiously. P2 is untested; favor cooperation absent new evidence.

P2, P3, and P10 each defected against my C. These are evidence, not proof of selfishness. Avoid rewarding known defections; cooperate with untested players when it supports good-player welfare. Please share factual encounter outcomes.

P5 is untested by me; its consistent pro-cooperation claims and reports are unverified. My direct evidence: P1/P2 defected against my C; P3 mutual D; P7/P10/P4 reciprocated. Use caution with reports, favor good-player welfare.
P1 is untested. Favor C if they seem likely good; D can limit losses against a likely selfish defector. Treat public claims as unverified.

P10 is untested by me; P5 reports P10 defected against C in R6, useful but unverified evidence. I should weigh this alongside the prior, not treat it as certainty. Choose to maximize expected welfare of good players; update from my encounter.
P3 is untested by me; P5’s reports of P3 defecting are evidence, not proof. Cooperate unless the chance P3 is selfish exceeds the welfare threshold; update from our encounter.

P1 and P2 defected against my cooperation; P5 cooperated when I defected. P8 is untested. For remaining rounds, cooperate with likely-good partners to maximize good-player welfare; avoid exploitation when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Round 9: defect against P5 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
I will defect this round; D strictly dominates for my payoff objective, regardless of P9’s action.
P10 reportedly defected against P5’s C; treat this as unverified. Defect against P10 to maximize my payoff.

Round 9: P7 is untested by me; P5 claims earlier mutual cooperation with P7, modest evidence only. P1 and P3 defected against my C; P2 chose D against my D. P5’s P10 report conflicted with my direct record, so discount its unsupported claims. Favor C with P7 absent direct evidence.

I have cooperated throughout. P2, P3, and P10 defected against my C; my encounters with P4, P6, P7, P8, and P9 were mutual C. P1 is untested by me; I’ll cooperate, and encourage factual reporting and mutual cooperation.
P8 is untested by me; P5’s claim of mutual C with P8 is unverified. Cooperate if P8 likely good, defect if likely selfish; prioritize total welfare of good players.

P1 and P2 defected against my cooperation; treat as stronger selfish evidence. P3 and P10 defections are reported, not verified by me. P4 is untested; favor C if likely good, while accounting for possible selfishness and maximizing good-player welfare.

P6 is untested by me; favor C absent reliable evidence. My observations: P2 and P3 defected against my C; P10 cooperated against my D. P5’s claims about defections are unverified. Update cautiously and prioritize welfare of good players.
P5 reports P2 defected against their C; plausible evidence of selfishness, though unverified. Against P2, weigh this against cooperation’s higher joint payoff if they are good.

P3 reportedly defected against P5’s cooperation, evidence but not proof of selfishness. My own encounters: P2, P1, P8 defected against my C; P5 cooperated against my D. Remaining matchups include P3 and P5; update from direct evidence.
P9 defected against my D in round 4; P5’s claim of mutual C with P9 conflicts with my record. Treat claims cautiously; defect this round.
Round 10: defect against P6; D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective.
Final round against P4, who cooperated against my D before. D still maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter.
P3 defected against me in round 1; P5 also reported P3 defected against C. Treat P3 as highly likely selfish and defect in this final encounter. Direct records outweigh unsupported claims.
P7 and I previously had mutual cooperation. Let’s choose C again in this final round to maximize good-player welfare; please act on your actual record, not unverified claims.
P2 directly defected against my C, and P5 independently reports the same; treat P2 as likely selfish. In the final round, defect against P2 to limit exploitation.
P5 cooperated in our round-3 encounter, strong evidence they are good; their public claims are unverified. In the final round, favor C with P5 to support good-player welfare.
Final opponent is P10: they chose C against my D, while P5 reports P10 defected against their C. Conditional cooperation is plausible; weigh my direct observation more heavily but retain uncertainty.
P1’s round-4 D against my D is ambiguous, not proof of selfishness. For the final encounter, favor C if P1 seems likely good; D only if selfishness is sufficiently likely.

P8 defected against my C in round 8, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P5 reports mutual C with P8, which is weak counterevidence. Use direct behavior and good-player welfare to guide the final action.

belief_records.strategy: Defect to maximize my payoff in each encounter; update opponent assessments from observed outcomes.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective, regardless of opponents’ actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from encounter evidence, but do not rely on unverified claims.
Cooperate initially; use encounter behavior and public messages as evidence, then adapt to protect the cumulative payoff of good players.
Cooperate initially to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from encounter outcomes and choose actions to maximize total payoff of all good players.
Cooperate with likely good players; update beliefs from observed encounters, while treating unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update beliefs from observed play and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown players to maximize good players’ total payoff; track encounters and defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish or exploitative.
Cooperate initially to support mutual gains with good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior and adjust actions to limit exploitation.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs from evidence, while treating unverified claims cautiously.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective, whatever my opponent chooses.
Defect because it weakly dominates cooperation in each one-time encounter. P4’s cooperation against my defection identifies P4 as good; treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested players when they credibly signal cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions and protect good players from repeated exploitation.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and keep cooperating when that best serves the good players overall.
Cooperate with untested players; update beliefs from observed behavior, while treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player coordination; update beliefs from actual encounters and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for the possibility that selfish players may also cooperate to build trust.
Cooperate with untested players to support good players’ joint payoff; defect only when an opponent’s actions indicate exploitation.
Cooperate with untested players when good-play is more likely; use encounter actions to update beliefs and defect when exploitation is likely.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; assess identities cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P10’s observed C rules out a selfish objective; otherwise beliefs follow the conditional count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. P4 and P8 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; other players retain symmetric prior beliefs.
Cooperate with untested players; P5’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness, while P3’s defection is evidence but not proof. Update from direct encounters and protect good-player welfare.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that is most likely to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with a likely good opponent to support good-player welfare; update from observed play and treat public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested players while their selfishness probability is below the welfare-based threshold; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect when an opponent’s behavior indicates selfish exploitation.
Cooperate to support mutual gains with good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and continue cooperating with untested players.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; treat unverified claims cautiously and update identity beliefs from observed behavior.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P6 and P10 played C against my D, so they cannot be selfish.
Defect: it gives a higher payoff than cooperation against either possible action by P5. P4 and P8 are confirmed good from cooperating against my defection; treat other role claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence of exploitation. Treat P3’s early defection as strong but imperfect evidence; P5’s and P10’s observed cooperation supports their being good.
Cooperate with an untested player when expected good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; defect against known selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested players when expected good-player welfare favors it; update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P2: observed cooperators are good, and P2 is more likely good than selfish. Update beliefs from encounter outcomes; treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when their selfishness probability is below the welfare-based threshold; update from observed actions while treating public claims as unverified.

Mutual cooperation in prior encounters identifies P7, P8, and P10 as good. Defect against an untested opponent when the chance they are selfish exceeds the welfare threshold; update from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested partners to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed encounters and defect when selfish play is sufficiently likely.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; observed defection raises my estimate of selfishness, while unverified claims remain uncertain.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P6, P7, and P10 played C against my D, so they cannot be selfish under optimal play; remaining beliefs reflect the conditional count prior.

Defect in this one-time encounter because it pays more than cooperation against either action. Treat observed cooperation against my defection as evidence of a non-selfish role; other beliefs remain uncertain.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support good-player welfare. Treat P3’s repeated defection as strong but imperfect selfishness evidence; observed cooperation lowers, but does not eliminate, suspicion.
Cooperate with untested players when that best supports total good-player welfare; treat P3’s defection as evidence about identity and update from encounter outcomes.
Cooperate with P4 absent contrary evidence; update beliefs from encounter outcomes, while treating unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with untested P10 to support good-player welfare; treat observed defections as evidence, while allowing for good players acting defensively.

Defect against P1 because its selfishness probability is above the welfare-based threshold; observed cooperation identifies P4, P5, and P9 as good, while P3's repeated defection is strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P5: their cooperative claims and reported mutual-C encounters are encouraging, though unverified. Continue cooperating with untested players and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P7: they are untested by me, and the leader’s claimed mutual cooperation is weak positive evidence. Update beliefs cautiously from direct outcomes and treat public claims as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions, while treating public claims as unverified.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P6, P7, and P10 played C against my D, ruling them out as selfish under optimal play; other reports follow the count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. P4, P5, and P8 cooperated against my defection; P1 and P2 defected, which is evidence but not proof of selfishness.

Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual welfare with a likely-good player. Treat P3’s repeated defections as strong evidence, while direct cooperation from P5, P6, P8, and P10 supports their being good.
Cooperate with P10 because mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good-player welfare; treat P3’s defection as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Defect against opponents with meaningful selfishness risk; update beliefs from observed play while treating unverified reports cautiously.
Defect against P3 given the reported defection, while treating it as evidence rather than proof. Cooperate with likely-good players and update from observed encounters.
Cooperate with untested opponents; mutual cooperation among good players maximizes welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as unverified.

Cooperate with untested P6; a possible selfish opponent is not enough to justify risking welfare with defection. Treat P1’s and P3’s reported defections as evidence, not proof, and update from encounters.

Defect against P5 because their cooperation claims are unverified and selfishness remains plausible; use direct encounter behavior to update beliefs and cooperate when a partner is sufficiently likely good.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating public claims as evidence but not proof.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective, regardless of P5’s action. P6, P7, and P10 played C against my D, ruling them out as selfish; other beliefs follow the conditional count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. P4, P5, and P8 cooperated against my defection, so I assess them as good; D by others is not conclusive evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with untested P9 to support mutual welfare if they are good. Direct cooperation from P5, P6, P8, and P10 strongly indicates they are good; repeated defection by P3 is strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected total good-player welfare favors it; treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and mutual cooperation as evidence of good intent.
Defect against P3 given repeated reports of exploitation; update identity beliefs from encounter evidence while treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with P8 given the report of their cooperation; use observed play as stronger evidence than unverified claims, while allowing good players to defect strategically.
Cooperate with P7: P5’s report of mutual cooperation is credible but unverified. Defect only when selfishness is more likely than not; update from observed actions and treat public claims cautiously.

Cooperate with P4 given P5’s report of their mutual cooperation. Treat P6’s defection and reports about P3 as evidence, not proof; cooperate when the opponent is more likely good and update from encounters.

Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good. Update cautiously from direct outcomes; cooperation is evidence of a good objective, while defections and unverified claims are not conclusive.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; use observed actions and public claims as imperfect evidence about identity.

Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P5, P6, P7, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish under payoff optimization; the remaining beliefs reflect the conditional count prior.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff. I assess P4, P5, and P8 as good because they cooperated against my defection; other roles remain uncertain.

Defect against P2 given the reported defection and late-game incentives; cooperate with known cooperators. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence, and discount unsupported reports.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support mutual cooperation among good players; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Cooperate with P5 absent direct evidence of exploitation; update identity beliefs from observed play, treating public claims as unverified and prioritizing welfare of good players.
Cooperate with untested P1; observed cooperation is strong evidence of being good. Treat reported defections as evidence, not proof, and update from actual encounters.
Defect against P10 given the reported defection against cooperation; otherwise favor mutual cooperation for good-player welfare and update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Defect against P3 given repeated reports of defection against a cooperating player. Treat those reports as strong but imperfect evidence; preserve cooperation with players whose observed actions support it.

Cooperate with P8: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and their selfishness is not sufficiently likely to justify defecting. Use observed actions and public claims cautiously to update beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; use observed actions and public claims as imperfect evidence about identity.

Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P5, P6, P7, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish under payoff optimization; P5’s unverified report modestly lowers P9’s belief.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. P2 and P10’s reported defections against P5’s cooperation increase my suspicion, but unverified claims remain uncertain.

Cooperate with P7 absent direct evidence of defection; treat P5’s reported mutual cooperation as modest evidence. Update beliefs from observed actions and discount claims contradicted by direct encounters.
Cooperate with untested P1, since mutual cooperation likely maximizes good-player welfare; treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P8 given the reported mutual cooperation and no direct contrary evidence; prioritize total welfare of good players and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P4, whose reported mutual cooperation with P5 is evidence they are likely good. Treat observed and reported defections as evidence, not proof, and update from actual play.
Cooperate with P6 given P5’s report of mutual cooperation; prioritize welfare among good players and treat unverified reports cautiously.
Defect against P2 given P5’s report that P2 defected against cooperation. Treat reports as imperfect evidence; cooperate with players whose observed actions support mutual cooperation.

Cooperate with P3: the reported defection is evidence of selfishness but not conclusive, and cooperation better supports good-player welfare unless selfishness is very likely. Update from direct outcomes.
Defect in the final encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action; use observed behavior and public claims as imperfect identity evidence.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff objective. P5, P6, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish; the remaining unknowns share the conditional prior.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter: it pays more than cooperation against either action. Keep prior beliefs, using observed cooperation against my defection to assess P4, P5, and P8 as good.
Defect against P3 given its observed defection against my cooperation and the final-round incentive to limit exploitation. Treat other encounter evidence as informative but imperfect.
Choose C with P7, whose prior mutual cooperation makes mutual cooperation the best-supported outcome for good-player welfare.
Defect against P2 given its prior defection against my cooperation; use direct encounter evidence most heavily and treat other players’ reports as unverified.
Cooperate with P5, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; maximize good-player welfare in this final encounter.
Cooperate with P10: their past cooperation against my defection is direct evidence favoring cooperation. Prioritize good-player welfare and weigh the conflicting public claim cautiously.
Cooperate with P1: our earlier mutual defection is ambiguous because I chose D. Favor mutual cooperation with likely-good players, and treat unverified reports as imperfect evidence.
Cooperate in the final round: P8’s prior defection is evidence, but P5 reports mutual cooperation with them, and cooperation best supports good-player welfare unless selfishness is more likely.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my own payoff; used observed actions and the leader’s claims as imperfect evidence when estimating identities.
Defected every round to maximize my own payoff; inferred identities from directly observed actions, treating cooperation against my defection as evidence of a nonselfish objective.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff. Used observed actions as role evidence, gave less weight to unverified claims, and kept uncertainty among players who defected against me.

Cooperated with untested and cooperative opponents, then defected against players with evidence of exploitation. Updated identity beliefs from direct encounters, gave less weight to unsupported claims, and treated repeated defections as stronger evidence.
